name: Sri Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy Temple, Yadadri
nativeName: శ్రీ లక్ష్మీ నరసింహ స్వామి ఆలయం, యాదాద్రి
deity: Vishnu as Lakshmi Narasimha, worshipped in his five forms (Pancha Narasimha) on the hill
period: A hill shrine of Narasimha in Telangana, sage Yadarshi's seat, lately rebuilt in stone on a grand scale
dynasty: Ancient tradition, reconstructed in Krishna stone in our own time
summary: On the Yadadri hill, Vishnu is worshipped as Lakshmi Narasimha in five forms, at a shrine said to have been won by the sage Yadarshi's penance and reborn in our time as a vast temple of black stone.

sections.history: Yadadri, or Yadagirigutta, crowns a hill in Telangana. Tradition holds that the sage Yadarshi, son of Rishyasringa, did penance here and was granted the vision of Narasimha in five forms; the god stayed on the hill as Lakshmi Narasimha. In recent years the temple has been rebuilt on a grand scale in black Krishna stone.
sections.architecture: The reborn temple rises in the Dravidian manner in dark stone, with towered gateways and carved halls, gathered around the cave-like sanctum where the five forms of Narasimha are worshipped. The hilltop setting and the black-stone mass give it a stern, ancient grandeur.
sections.legends: The five forms — Jwala, Yogananda, Gandabherunda, Ugra, and Lakshmi Narasimha — are held to have revealed themselves to Yadarshi in a cave on the hill. Narasimha, the man-lion who tore apart the demon Hiranyakashipu to save the child Prahlada, is here the fierce yet grace-giving lord of the hill.
sections.festivals: Brahmotsavam and the days of Narasimha, above all Narasimha Jayanti, fill the hill with pilgrims. The temple is also sought for the rites that calm the fierce aspect of the god and heal affliction.
sections.experience: Yadadri joins the awe of a hill-shrine of the fierce Narasimha with the freshness of a temple newly raised in stone — a pilgrimage both ancient in spirit and new to the eye.

visit.timings: Open daily with morning and evening darshan and a midday break; Narasimha Jayanti and Brahmotsavam are busiest. Confirm current timings before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear removed before entering. Follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.photography: Photography is restricted in and around the sanctum; follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.gettingThere: Yadadri lies in Yadadri Bhuvanagiri district of Telangana, reached by road from Hyderabad, with the nearest railhead at Raigir/Bhongir.
